spans.s: उभ [ubha], pron. a. (Used only in the dual) Both; उभौ तौ न विजानीतः
; Śi.3.8. [cf. Zend. uba.; Gr.amphi; L. ambo].
उभय [ubhaya], pron. a. (-यी f.) (Though dual in sense, it is used in the singular and plural only; according to some grammarians in the dual also) Both (of persons or things); यस्तद्वेदोभयं सह Īśa.

,-Comp. -अन्वयिन् a. Tending towards both, keeping connection with both. -अलंकारः (in Rhet.) A figure of speech, which sets off both the sense and sound. -अर्थम्ind. for a double object (for earthly prosperity and heavenly happiness also). -आत्मक a. belonging to both. -चर a. living in water and on land or in the air, amphibious. Mātaṅga
. (-रः) a class of birds who live both on land and in the air. -च्छन्ना (in Rhet.) A kind of enigma. -द्युः ind.
the day past and to come. -पदिन् a. Having both Parasmai and Atmane pada. -भागहर a.

taking two shares. (-रम्) a medicine that acts in two ways (both as an emetic and a purgative). -मुख a. two faced; a pregnant female.-विद्या two-fold sciences; i. e. religious knowledge and knowledge about worldly affairs. -विध a. of both kinds. -विपुला f. N. f a metre. -विभ्रष्ट a. losing both कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टः
. -वेतन a. receiving wages from both (parties), serving two masters, treacherous, perfidious; उभयवेतनो भूत्वा

. -व्यञ्जन a. having the marks of both sexes, hermaphrodite. -संभवः a. dilemma. -स्नातक a. one who has performed the prescribed ablutions after finishing both his time of studying and his vow. See Kullūka on
उभया [ubhayā], ind. Ved. In both ways; बृहस्पतिर्व उभया न मृळात्
. -Comp. -दत् a. having teeth on both sides. -विन् a. being on both sides, partaking of both. -हस्ति ind. as much as may be grasped with both hands; उभयाहस्त्या भर
From both sides, on both sides, to both sides (with acc.) एतदनृतमुभयतः सत्येन परिगृहीतम् Br.
उभयतः कृष्णं गोपाः Sk. तज्जाः पुनात्युभयतः पुरुषा- नेकविंशतिम्
In both ways; पुष्पिणः फलिनश्चैव वृक्षास्तूभयतः स्मृताः
.-Comp. -क्षुत् a. two-edged (Ved.). -दत्, -दन्त a. having a double row of teeth; पशून् मृगान् मनुष्यांश्च व्यालाश्चो- भयतोदतः
